newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey cabinet to discuss army Islamist demands.
newsitem.headline: Turkey cabinet to discuss army Islamist demands.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led cabinet meets on Thursday to discuss an army push to curb religious activism and return the country to rigid secularism.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's office said in a statement that the meeting would begin at 1000 GMT. Islamist Erbakan said on Wednesday night the cabinet was willing to carry out some anti-Islamist demands from the military.
"All requests will be taken into consideration. The ones that are in line with the constitution and the laws will be carried out," Anatolian news agency quoted him as saying.
But he said civilian authorities were not obliged to take orders from the military-dominated National Security Council (MGK), which demanded the crackdown late last month.
"The MGK is not above parliament and the cabinet," he said. Turkish ministers have traditionally rubber-stamped decisions by the influential council.
Political analysts say Erbakan will probably give concessions to the army at the cabinet meeting on demands that he does not see as directly affecting his grassroots support.

Coalition partner Tansu Ciller, a pro-Western secularist, is expected to push the prime minister for wide implementation of the measures wanted by the army, which include enforcing a ban on Islamic dress and restricting religious education.
